<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">To obtain the form in Eq. (<a href="#A2.E16" title="Equation 16 ‣ Lemma B.1. ‣ B.2.1 Probability at the Boundaries ‣ B.2 Boundary behaviour of the Normalized Two-Sided 2x2PL Model ‣ Appendix B Two-sided 2PL propensity model: additional details ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>), let <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=e^{-a^{\prime}r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=e^{-a^{\prime}r}</annotation></semantics></math>, so that <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a^{\prime}r)=(1+t)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a^{\prime}r)=(1+t)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(2a^{\prime}r)=(1+t^{2})^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(2a^{\prime}r)=(1+t^{2})^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{(1+t)^{2}}{2(1+t^{2})}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{(1+t)^{2}}{2(1+t^{2})}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Observing that</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a^{\prime}r)^{2}+(1-\sigma(a^{\prime}r))^{2}=\frac{1}{(1+t)^{2}}+\frac{t^{2}}{(1+t)^{2}}=\frac{1+t^{2}}{(1+t)^{2}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a^{\prime}r)^{2}+(1-\sigma(a^{\prime}r))^{2}=\frac{1}{(1+t)^{2}}+\frac{t^{2}}{(1+t)^{2}}=\frac{1+t^{2}}{(1+t)^{2}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">we obtain Eq. (<a href="#A2.E16" title="Equation 16 ‣ Lemma B.1. ‣ B.2.1 Probability at the Boundaries ‣ B.2 Boundary behaviour of the Normalized Two-Sided 2x2PL Model ‣ Appendix B Two-sided 2PL propensity model: additional details ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>).
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.2 </span>behaviour as the Interval Width Approaches Zero</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now show that as the propensity demand interval shrinks to a single point, the boundary probability converges to exactly <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem B.2</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">As <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to 0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to 0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{r\to 0^{+}}P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{r\to 0^{+}}P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">As <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to 0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to 0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, hence <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{1/r}\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{1/r}\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}=a+e^{1/r}-1\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}=a+e^{1/r}-1\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">To determine the behaviour of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r</annotation></semantics></math>, note that</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r=ar+re^{1/r}-r." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r=ar+re^{1/r}-r.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Setting <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1/r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1/r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="re^{1/r}=e^{t}/t\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">re^{1/r}=e^{t}/t\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(x)\to 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(x)\to 1</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\to 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\to 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and therefore:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{r\to 0^{+}}P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\lim_{r\to 0^{+}}\frac{1}{2[\sigma(a^{\prime}r)^{2}+(1-\sigma(a^{\prime}r))^{2}]}=\frac{1}{2[1+0]}=\frac{1}{2}.\qed" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">.</mo><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_italic" lspace="0.0835em" mathvariant="italic" separator="true">∎</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{r\to 0^{+}}P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\lim_{r\to 0^{+}}\frac{1}{2[\sigma(a^{\prime}r)^{2}+(1-\sigma(a^{\prime}r))^{2}]}=\frac{1}{2[1+0]}=\frac{1}{2}.\qed</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The convergence rate is characterized by the following expansion.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition B.3</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">As <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to 0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to 0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}+e^{-a^{\prime}r}+O(e^{-3a^{\prime}r})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}+e^{-a^{\prime}r}+O(e^{-3a^{\prime}r}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{-a^{\prime}r}=O(\exp(-re^{1/r}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-a^{\prime}r}=O(\exp(-re^{1/r}))</annotation></semantics></math> decays faster than any polynomial in <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u=a^{\prime}r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u=a^{\prime}r</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon=e^{-u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon=e^{-u}</annotation></semantics></math>. As <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to 0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to 0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>. From Eq. (<a href="#A2.E17" title="Equation 17 ‣ Proof. ‣ B.2.1 Probability at the Boundaries ‣ B.2 Boundary behaviour of the Normalized Two-Sided 2x2PL Model ‣ Appendix B Two-sided 2PL propensity model: additional details ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>) with <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=e^{-u}=\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=e^{-u}=\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{(1+\epsilon)^{2}}{2(1+\epsilon^{2})}=\frac{1+2\epsilon+\epsilon^{2}}{2(1+\epsilon^{2})}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{(1+\epsilon)^{2}}{2(1+\epsilon^{2})}=\frac{1+2\epsilon+\epsilon^{2}}{2(1+\epsilon^{2})}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">Expanding <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1+\epsilon^{2})^{-1}=1-\epsilon^{2}+O(\epsilon^{4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1+\epsilon^{2})^{-1}=1-\epsilon^{2}+O(\epsilon^{4})</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">For the decay rate, note that <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r=ar+re^{1/r}-r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r=ar+re^{1/r}-r</annotation></semantics></math>, where the dominant term is <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="re^{1/r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">re^{1/r}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{-a^{\prime}r}=O(\exp(-re^{1/r}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-a^{\prime}r}=O(\exp(-re^{1/r}))</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="re^{1/r}=e^{t}/t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">re^{1/r}=e^{t}/t</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1/r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1/r</annotation></semantics></math>, this term grows faster than any polynomial in <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1/r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1/r</annotation></semantics></math>, implying <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{-a^{\prime}r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-a^{\prime}r}</annotation></semantics></math> decays faster than any polynomial in <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.3 </span>behaviour as the Interval Width Grows Large</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next consider the opposite regime, corresponding to one of the boundaries becoming inactive (i.e., <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{l}\to-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{l}\to-\infty</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{u}\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{u}\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem B.4</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">As <math id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{r\to+\infty}P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{r\to+\infty}P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">As <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{1/r}\to 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{1/r}\to 1</annotation></semantics></math>, hence <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}=a+e^{1/r}-1\to a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}=a+e^{1/r}-1\to a</annotation></semantics></math>. Furthermore, <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\to 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\to 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Applying Lemma <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma B.1. ‣ B.2.1 Probability at the Boundaries ‣ B.2 Boundary behaviour of the Normalized Two-Sided 2x2PL Model ‣ Appendix B Two-sided 2PL propensity model: additional details ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{r\to+\infty}P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2[1+0]}=\frac{1}{2}.\qed" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">.</mo><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_italic" lspace="0.0835em" mathvariant="italic" separator="true">∎</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{r\to+\infty}P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2[1+0]}=\frac{1}{2}.\qed</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div id="A2.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition B.5</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">As <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}+e^{-ar-1}\left(1-\frac{1}{2r}+O(r^{-2})\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}+e^{-ar-1}\left(1-\frac{1}{2r}+O(r^{-2})\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=1/r\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=1/r\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. From Lemma <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma B.1. ‣ B.2.1 Probability at the Boundaries ‣ B.2 Boundary behaviour of the Normalized Two-Sided 2x2PL Model ‣ Appendix B Two-sided 2PL propensity model: additional details ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>, we have:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{(1+t)^{2}}{2(1+t^{2})}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{(1+t)^{2}}{2(1+t^{2})},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=e^{-a^{\prime}r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=e^{-a^{\prime}r}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 1: Expand <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r</annotation></semantics></math>.<span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Taylor expanding <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{\delta}=1+\delta+\delta^{2}/2+O(\delta^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>δ</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{\delta}=1+\delta+\delta^{2}/2+O(\delta^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}=a+e^{\delta}-1=a+\delta+\frac{\delta^{2}}{2}+O(\delta^{3})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>δ</mi></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}=a+e^{\delta}-1=a+\delta+\frac{\delta^{2}}{2}+O(\delta^{3}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore:</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 2: Expand <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=e^{-a^{\prime}r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=e^{-a^{\prime}r}</annotation></semantics></math>.<span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p5.1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></p>

<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">Using <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{-x}=1-x+O(x^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-x}=1-x+O(x^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> for small <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 3: Expand the boundary probability.<span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p6.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Since <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, we expand:</span></span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1+t)^{2}=1+2t+t^{2},\qquad(1+t^{2})^{-1}=1-t^{2}+O(t^{4})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1+t)^{2}=1+2t+t^{2},\qquad(1+t^{2})^{-1}=1-t^{2}+O(t^{4}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex24.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}(1+2t+t^{2})(1-t^{2}+O(t^{4}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}(1+2t+t^{2})(1-t^{2}+O(t^{4}))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
