<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}+t+O(t^{3})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}+t+O(t^{3}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 4: Substitute and simplify.<span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Substituting the expansion for <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}+e^{-ar-1}\left(1-\frac{1}{2r}+O(r^{-2})\right)+O(e^{-3(ar+1)})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}+e^{-ar-1}\left(1-\frac{1}{2r}+O(r^{-2})\right)+O(e^{-3(ar+1)}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7.2.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{-3ar}=o(e^{-ar}/r^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-3ar}=o(e^{-ar}/r^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, the <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(t^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(t^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> term is absorbed into the error, yielding:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}+e^{-ar-1}\left(1-\frac{1}{2r}+O(r^{-2})\right).\qed" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">.</mo><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_italic" lspace="0.0835em" mathvariant="italic" separator="true">∎</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\frac{1}{2}+e^{-ar-1}\left(1-\frac{1}{2r}+O(r^{-2})\right).\qed</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.4 </span>Uniform Bounds for Fixed Discrimination</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we establish explicit bounds on the boundary probability that hold uniformly over all interval widths for a fixed base discrimination parameter <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem B.6</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=1</annotation></semantics></math> and all <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{2}\leq P_{\mathrm{boundary}}\leq\frac{1}{2[\sigma(e)^{2}+(1-\sigma(e))^{2}]}\approx 0.5657." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.5657</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\leq P_{\mathrm{boundary}}\leq\frac{1}{2[\sigma(e)^{2}+(1-\sigma(e))^{2}]}\approx 0.5657.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">When <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=1</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}=e^{1/r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}=e^{1/r}</annotation></semantics></math> and thus <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r=re^{1/r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r=re^{1/r}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 1: Show that <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="re^{1/r}\geq e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">re^{1/r}\geq e</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.<span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Define <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(r)=re^{1/r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(r)=re^{1/r}</annotation></semantics></math>. Taking logarithms: <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ln g(r)=\ln r+1/r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln g(r)=\ln r+1/r</annotation></semantics></math>. Differentiating:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{d}{dr}(\ln r+1/r)=\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{r^{2}}=\frac{r-1}{r^{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>r</mi></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dr}(\ln r+1/r)=\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{r^{2}}=\frac{r-1}{r^{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">This derivative is negative for <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, zero at <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=1</annotation></semantics></math>, and positive for <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=1</annotation></semantics></math> is a global minimum with <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(1)=1\cdot e^{1}=e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(1)=1\cdot e^{1}=e</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r=re^{1/r}\geq e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r=re^{1/r}\geq e</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 2: Analise <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}</annotation></semantics></math> as a function of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a^{\prime}r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a^{\prime}r)</annotation></semantics></math>.<span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p5.1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Define <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(s)=s^{2}+(1-s)^{2}=2s^{2}-2s+1=2(s-1/2)^{2}+1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(s)=s^{2}+(1-s)^{2}=2s^{2}-2s+1=2(s-1/2)^{2}+1/2</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. This function achieves its minimum value of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=1/2</annotation></semantics></math> and is strictly increasing on <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1/2,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1/2,1)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(1)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(1)=1</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r\geq e&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r\geq e&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a^{\prime}r)&gt;1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a^{\prime}r)&gt;1/2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=[2h(\sigma(a^{\prime}r))]^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}=[2h(\sigma(a^{\prime}r))]^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 3: Establish the bounds.<span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p8.1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Lower bound:</span><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.1.2" class="ltx_text"> As <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math> (which occurs as <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to 0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to 0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>), we have <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\to 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\to 1</annotation></semantics></math>, hence <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(\sigma(a^{\prime}r))\to 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(\sigma(a^{\prime}r))\to 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}\to 1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}\to 1/2</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}&gt;1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}&gt;1/2</annotation></semantics></math> for all finite <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Upper bound:</span><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.1.2" class="ltx_text"> The minimum value of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>, attained at <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing on <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1/2,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1/2,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the maximum of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}</annotation></semantics></math> occurs when <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r</annotation></semantics></math> is minimized, i.e., when <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r=e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r=e</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\max}=\frac{1}{2[\sigma(e)^{2}+(1-\sigma(e))^{2}]}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\max}=\frac{1}{2[\sigma(e)^{2}+(1-\sigma(e))^{2}]}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.2.1" class="ltx_text">Numerically, <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(e)=(1+e^{-e})^{-1}\approx 0.9380" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.9380</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(e)=(1+e^{-e})^{-1}\approx 0.9380</annotation></semantics></math>, giving:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex32.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(e)^{2}+(1-\sigma(e))^{2}\approx 0.8799+0.0038=0.8837," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>0.8799</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0038</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8837</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(e)^{2}+(1-\sigma(e))^{2}\approx 0.8799+0.0038=0.8837,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.3.1" class="ltx_text">and thus <math id="A2.SS2.SSS4.p10.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\max}\approx 1/(2\times 0.8837)\approx 0.5657" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>0.8837</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.5657</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\max}\approx 1/(2\times 0.8837)\approx 0.5657</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Remark B.7</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem6" title="Theorem B.6. ‣ B.2.4 Uniform Bounds for Fixed Discrimination ‣ B.2 Boundary behaviour of the Normalized Two-Sided 2x2PL Model ‣ Appendix B Two-sided 2PL propensity model: additional details ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a> can be generalized to arbitrary <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. For general <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, the function <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(r)=a^{\prime}r=ar+re^{1/r}-r=(a-1)r+re^{1/r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(r)=a^{\prime}r=ar+re^{1/r}-r=(a-1)r+re^{1/r}</annotation></semantics></math> has its minimum at some <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{*}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{*}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> depending on <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>. The upper bound on <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\mathrm{boundary}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>boundary</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\mathrm{boundary}}</annotation></semantics></math> is then determined by evaluating the model at <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r=f(r^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r=f(r^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.5 </span>Summary</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The results of this appendix are summarized in Table <a href="#A2.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ B.2.5 Summary ‣ B.2 Boundary behaviour of the Normalized Two-Sided 2x2PL Model ‣ Appendix B Two-sided 2PL propensity model: additional details ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A2.T5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 5</span>: </span><span id="A2.T5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Boundary probability behaviour under different limiting regimes.</span></figcaption>

<tr id="A2.T5.5.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T5.5.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><math id="A2.T5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=1</annotation></semantics></math>, all <math id="A2.T5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A2.T5.5.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="A2.T5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\in[0.5,0.566]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.566</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\in[0.5,0.566]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A2.T5.5.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb">—</td></tr>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These results confirm that the normalisation scheme in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ 3.2 Propensities: the two-sided 2x2PL Model ‣ 3 Conceptualisation ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) successfully maintains the boundary interpretation: the propensity demand bounds <math id="A2.SS2.SSS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{u}</annotation></semantics></math> correspond approximately to <math id="A2.SS2.SSS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50\%</annotation></semantics></math> success probability, consistent with the interpretation of the difficulty parameter in the standard 2PL model for capabilities.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Propensity estimation via maximum likelihood</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> items <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(b_{l,i},b_{u,i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(b_{l,i},b_{u,i})</annotation></semantics></math> and outcomes <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the log-likelihood for <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is given
in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E6" title="Equation 6 ‣ 3.2 Propensities: the two-sided 2x2PL Model ‣ 3 Conceptualisation ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>) (main paper). Expanding the terms explicitly (with item-specific <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}_{i},A_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}_{i},A_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>
induced by <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(b_{l,i},b_{u,i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(b_{l,i},b_{u,i})</annotation></semantics></math>) gives</p>
<table id="A2.EGx5" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_eqnarray ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex34"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\ell(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\ell(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex33.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>=</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex33.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{N}\Big[y_{i}\cdot\log\!\Big(A_{i}\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}_{i}\cdot(\theta-b_{l,i}))\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}_{i}\cdot(b_{u,i}-\theta))\Big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mpadded style="width:1.146em;" width="1.146em"><mi>log</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{N}\Big[y_{i}\cdot\log\!\Big(A_{i}\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}_{i}\cdot(\theta-b_{l,i}))\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}_{i}\cdot(b_{u,i}-\theta))\Big)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr>
<tr class="ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex34.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\qquad\quad+(1-y_{i})\cdot\log\!\Big(1-A_{i}\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}_{i}\cdot(\theta-b_{l,i}))\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}_{i}\cdot(b_{u,i}-\theta))\Big)\Big]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mpadded style="width:1.146em;" width="1.146em"><mi>log</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\qquad\quad+(1-y_{i})\cdot\log\!\Big(1-A_{i}\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}_{i}\cdot(\theta-b_{l,i}))\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}_{i}\cdot(b_{u,i}-\theta))\Big)\Big].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The maximum likelihood estimator is simply <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\arg\max_{\theta}\;\ell(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>max</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arg\max_{\theta}\;\ell(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>. However, this cannot be solved analytically, and numerical (gradient-based) optimisation is needed.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To initialise the numerical optimiser, we consider the empirical (observed) success probability curve:</p>
<table id="A2.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E18.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{P}_{\mathrm{emp}}(b_{l},b_{u})=\frac{\sum_{i:(b_{l,i},b_{u,i})=(b_{l},b_{u})}y_{i}}{\sum_{i:(b_{l,i},b_{u,i})=(b_{l},b_{u})}1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>emp</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}_{\mathrm{emp}}(b_{l},b_{u})=\frac{\sum_{i:(b_{l,i},b_{u,i})=(b_{l},b_{u})}y_{i}}{\sum_{i:(b_{l,i},b_{u,i})=(b_{l},b_{u})}1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">This lives naturally in the 2D window space and corresponds to a characteristic <em id="A2.SS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">surface</em>.
From this, a simple pointwise collapse averaging outcomes over all windows that contain a point <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> can be defined:</p>
<table id="A2.Ex35" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex35.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{P}_{\mathrm{point}}(x)=\frac{\sum_{i:\,b_{l,i}\leq x\leq b_{u,i}}y_{i}}{\sum_{i:\,b_{l,i}\leq x\leq b_{u,i}}1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>point</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.448em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></msub><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.448em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></msub><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}_{\mathrm{point}}(x)=\frac{\sum_{i:\,b_{l,i}\leq x\leq b_{u,i}}y_{i}}{\sum_{i:\,b_{l,i}\leq x\leq b_{u,i}}1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">While maximising <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}_{\mathrm{point}}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>point</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}_{\mathrm{point}}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is not an unbiased estimator of <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, we use it to provide an initial guess for MLE. Figure <a href="#A2.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ B.3 Propensity estimation via maximum likelihood ‣ Appendix B Two-sided 2PL propensity model: additional details ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> shows the empirical curve <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{P}_{\mathrm{point}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>point</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{P}_{\mathrm{point}}</annotation></semantics></math> as well as the value obtained with MLE.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18182v1/Figures/empirical-2D.png" id="A2.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:286/226;" width="286" height="226" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="A2.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Empirical collapse for the case in Fig. <a href="#A2.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ B.1 Additional visualisations ‣ Appendix B Two-sided 2PL propensity model: additional details ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>: a non-parametric fit peaks at
<math id="A2.F6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1.091" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.091</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.091</annotation></semantics></math> (prob. <math id="A2.F6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.831" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.831</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.831</annotation></semantics></math>), far from the true <math id="A2.F6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=-1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=-1.5</annotation></semantics></math>. MLE yields <math id="A2.F6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\theta}=-1.514" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.514</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\theta}=-1.514</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Capabilities as a Special Case of the Propensities Model</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now establish rigorously that the two-sided propensity model subsumes the standard monotonic 2PL capability model as a limiting case. We prove this first for the unnormalized model (Eq. <a href="#S3.E2" title="Equation 2 ‣ 3.2 Propensities: the two-sided 2x2PL Model ‣ 3 Conceptualisation ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) and then for the normalized model (Eq. <a href="#S3.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ 3.2 Propensities: the two-sided 2x2PL Model ‣ 3 Conceptualisation ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem B.8</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Unnormalized Model Convergence)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta,b_{l},a_{l},a_{u}\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta,b_{l},a_{l},a_{u}\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{l},a_{u}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{l},a_{u}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> be fixed. Consider the unnormalized two-sided 2x2PL response function:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a_{l},a_{u})=\sigma(a_{l}(\theta-b_{l}))\cdot\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a_{l},a_{u})=\sigma(a_{l}(\theta-b_{l}))\cdot\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta)).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then:</span></p>
<ol id="A2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">As </span><math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{u}\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{u}\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">As </span><math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{l}\to-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{l}\to-\infty</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{b_{l}\to-\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a_{l},a_{u})=\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b_{l}\to-\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a_{l},a_{u})=\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta)).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">In particular, when the upper (resp. lower) boundary constraint is removed, the model reduces to the standard 2PL model with difficulty parameter <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b=b_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b=b_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> (resp. <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{u}</annotation></semantics></math>) and discrimination <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=a_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=a_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> (resp. <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{u}</annotation></semantics></math>).</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We prove each statement separately.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Proof of (i).</span>
Since <math id="A2.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{u}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{u}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> are fixed, we have:</p>
<table id="A2.E22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta)=a_{u}b_{u}-a_{u}\theta\to+\infty\quad\text{as }b_{u}\to+\infty." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mtext>as </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta)=a_{u}b_{u}-a_{u}\theta\to+\infty\quad\text{as }b_{u}\to+\infty.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(22)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.p3.2" class="ltx_p">By the definition of the sigmoid function <math id="A2.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(x)=(1+e^{-x})^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(x)=(1+e^{-x})^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{x\to+\infty}\sigma(x)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x\to+\infty}\sigma(x)=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore:</p>
<table id="A2.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))=1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))=1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(23)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.p3.3" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="A2.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a_{l}(\theta-b_{l}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a_{l}(\theta-b_{l}))</annotation></semantics></math> does not depend on <math id="A2.SS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{u}</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain:</p>
<table id="A2.EGx6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.E24"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a_{l},a_{u})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a_{l},a_{u})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E24.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}\sigma(a_{l}(\theta-b_{l}))\cdot\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}\sigma(a_{l}(\theta-b_{l}))\cdot\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
