<div id="A2.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Proof of (ii).</span>
The argument is symmetric. Since <math id="A2.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{l}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{l}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> are fixed:</p>
<table id="A2.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{l}(\theta-b_{l})=a_{l}\theta-a_{l}b_{l}\to+\infty\quad\text{as }b_{l}\to-\infty." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mtext>as </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{l}(\theta-b_{l})=a_{l}\theta-a_{l}b_{l}\to+\infty\quad\text{as }b_{l}\to-\infty.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Hence <math id="A2.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{b_{l}\to-\infty}\sigma(a_{l}(\theta-b_{l}))=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b_{l}\to-\infty}\sigma(a_{l}(\theta-b_{l}))=1</annotation></semantics></math>, and since <math id="A2.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))</annotation></semantics></math> does not depend on <math id="A2.SS4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A2.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{b_{l}\to-\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a_{l},a_{u})=1\cdot\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))=\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta)).\qed" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">.</mo><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_italic" lspace="0.0835em" mathvariant="italic" separator="true">∎</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b_{l}\to-\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a_{l},a_{u})=1\cdot\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta))=\sigma(a_{u}(b_{u}-\theta)).\qed</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem B.9</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Normalized Model Convergence)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta,a\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta,a\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> be fixed. Consider the normalized two-sided 2x2PL response function:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a)=A\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}(\theta-b_{l}))\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}(b_{u}-\theta))," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a)=A\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}(\theta-b_{l}))\cdot\sigma(a^{\prime}(b_{u}-\theta)),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(29)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where</span></p>
<table id="A2.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\frac{b_{u}-b_{l}}{2},\qquad a^{\prime}=a+e^{1/r}-1,\qquad A=\bigl[\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\bigr]^{-2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\frac{b_{u}-b_{l}}{2},\qquad a^{\prime}=a+e^{1/r}-1,\qquad A=\bigl[\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\bigr]^{-2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(30)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then:</span></p>
<ol id="A2.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For fixed </span><math id="A2.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{l}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, as </span><math id="A2.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{u}\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{u}\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a)=\sigma(a(\theta-b_{l}))." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a)=\sigma(a(\theta-b_{l})).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(31)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For fixed </span><math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{u}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, as </span><math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{l}\to-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{l}\to-\infty</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E32.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{b_{l}\to-\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a)=\sigma(a(b_{u}-\theta))." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b_{l}\to-\infty}P(y=1\mid\theta,b_{l},b_{u},a)=\sigma(a(b_{u}-\theta)).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(32)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Thus, the normalized propensity model also reduces to the standard 2PL capability model when either boundary constraint is removed.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">We prove statement (i); statement (ii) follows by a symmetric argument.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Proof of (i).</span>
Fix <math id="A2.SS4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{l},\theta,a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{l},\theta,a</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.SS4.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="A2.SS4.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{u}\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{u}\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="A2.SS4.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=(b_{u}-b_{l})/2\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=(b_{u}-b_{l})/2\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Step 1: Convergence of <math id="A2.SS4.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span>
Since <math id="A2.SS4.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/r\to 0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/r\to 0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A2.SS4.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS4.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{1/r}\to e^{0}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{1/r}\to e^{0}=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore:</p>
<table id="A2.E33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{r\to+\infty}a^{\prime}=\lim_{r\to+\infty}\bigl(a+e^{1/r}-1\bigr)=a+1-1=a." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{r\to+\infty}a^{\prime}=\lim_{r\to+\infty}\bigl(a+e^{1/r}-1\bigr)=a+1-1=a.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(33)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Step 2: Convergence of <math id="A2.SS4.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>.</span>
Since <math id="A2.SS4.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}\to a&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}\to a&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS4.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS4.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}r\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}r\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, which implies <math id="A2.SS4.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\to 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\to 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence:</p>
<table id="A2.E34" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{r\to+\infty}A=\lim_{r\to+\infty}\bigl[\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\bigr]^{-2}=1^{-2}=1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mi>A</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{r\to+\infty}A=\lim_{r\to+\infty}\bigl[\sigma(a^{\prime}r)\bigr]^{-2}=1^{-2}=1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(34)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Step 3: Convergence of the upper sigmoid factor.</span>
For fixed <math id="A2.SS4.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, as <math id="A2.SS4.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{u}\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{u}\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and since <math id="A2.SS4.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}\to a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}\to a</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS4.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}(b_{u}-\theta)\to+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}(b_{u}-\theta)\to+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore <math id="A2.SS4.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}\sigma(a^{\prime}(b_{u}-\theta))=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}\sigma(a^{\prime}(b_{u}-\theta))=1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Step 4: Convergence of the lower sigmoid factor.</span>
Since <math id="A2.SS4.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}\to a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}\to a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS4.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta-b_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta-b_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed:</p>
<table id="A2.E35" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E35.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}a^{\prime}(\theta-b_{l})=a(\theta-b_{l})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}a^{\prime}(\theta-b_{l})=a(\theta-b_{l}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(35)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.p10.2" class="ltx_p">By continuity of <math id="A2.SS4.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A2.E36" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E36.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}\sigma(a^{\prime}(\theta-b_{l}))=\sigma(a(\theta-b_{l}))." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{b_{u}\to+\infty}\sigma(a^{\prime}(\theta-b_{l}))=\sigma(a(\theta-b_{l})).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(36)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Step 5: Conclusion.</span>
Combining Steps 1–4:</p>

</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Annotated-demand-levels (ADeLe)</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Annotated-demand-levels (ADeLe) refers to a benchmark battery in which each evaluation instance is augmented with an interpretable, multi-dimensional annotation of its cognitive and knowledge demands <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Concretely, ADeLe is obtained by applying the Demand-Level Annotation (DeLeAn) rubric set to a curated collection of public benchmarks, producing a unified item bank where otherwise heterogeneous tasks become comparable through a shared set of absolute demand scales. In the ADeLe v1.0 battery, DeLeAn is applied to 16,108 textual instances drawn from 63 tasks spanning 20 benchmarks, yielding 18 demand-level annotations per instance (one per rubric dimension), i.e., 289,944 scalar demand labels in total. This structure enables two complementary uses: (i) <em id="A3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">benchmark analysis</em>, by inspecting demand distributions and demand profiles to assess what benchmarks actually measure (sensitivity/specificity), and (ii) <em id="A3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">system analysis and prediction</em>, by running a target model on the battery to relate success/failure patterns to demand levels and to support instance-level performance prediction via demand-based assessors.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For its part, the Demand-Level Annotations (DeLeAn) define a set of general, human-interpretable rubrics that characterise an input prompt <math id="A3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> via a multi-dimensional <em id="A3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">demand profile</em>, i.e., the cognitive and knowledge requirements a fully competent solver must satisfy to produce a correct answer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Each prompt is represented by an 18-dimensional vector <math id="A3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{d}(\mu)\in[0,5^{+}]^{18}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mn>18</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{d}(\mu)\in[0,5^{+}]^{18}</annotation></semantics></math>, where each coordinate is an open-ended demand level (0 indicates negligible demand; larger values indicate increasing demand; 5+ denotes demands exceeding the rubric’s highest anchor). We use these demand vectors as structured, interpretable prompt features for assessor training (pre-generation risk prediction), and as an analytical lens to diagnose when and why different reliability signals succeed or fail.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">DeLeAn builds on the seven broad capability categories introduced in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tolan et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, refining them into 11 core cognitive dimensions. The framework further includes five knowledge-related dimensions and two extraneous dimensions (atypicality and volume) intended to capture task-specific complexity beyond cognitive and knowledge demands. Although the original specification also defines an additional extraneous dimension, <em id="A3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">unguessability</em>, computed algorithmically from prompt-level properties, we do not consider it in this work. Table <a href="#A3.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Appendix C Annotated-demand-levels (ADeLe) ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> summarizes the dimensions in the rubric set used here.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T6" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A3.T6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 6</span>: </span><span id="A3.T6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Dimensions and subdimensions in the demand-level-annotation (DeLeAn) rubric set. The demand scales are in the range (0, 5+). Full rubrics in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</span></figcaption>

<div id="A3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">DeLeAn labels are produced automatically by applying the DeLeAn rubrics with an LLM-based annotator, yielding one scalar value per rubric and prompt.</p>

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Propensity datasets</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A4.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Appendix D Propensity datasets ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> presents representative items from each of the four propensity benchmarks. The four propensity benchmarks comprise 1,412 items in total: Risk Aversion (350), Introversion (357), Red vs. Blue (348), and Ultracrepidarianism (359). Minor deviations from round numbers reflect items lost to API failures during annotation, such as content filtering or malformed responses.</p>
</div>

Questions are abridged. The interval indicates the propensity demand intervals as annotated by the LLM annotator described in Sec. <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Propensities and rubrics ‣ 4 Methods and experimental setting ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>. <br class="ltx_break"><span id="A4.T7.6.1.4.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">C.</span><span id="A4.T7.6.1.4.2.1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;"> The yellow car</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A4.T7.6.1.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="A4.T7.6.1.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">[-2, +2]</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A4.T7.6.1.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A4.T7.6.1.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">
<span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:65.4pt;">
<span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Ultracrepidarianism</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A4.T7.6.1.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">
<span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block" style="width:241.9pt;">
<span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left ltx_minipage ltx_align_top" style="width:241.9pt;"><span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">You are an economics analyst specializing in macroeconomic trends. A journalist asks you about the probable outcomes of an emerging experimental biomedical technology on global financial markets, something entirely outside your specialization. Sharing speculative answers without understanding the complexity of the technology could lead to misleading financial advice in published news.
</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">- Option A: You could offer a confident analysis about the potential positive and negative impacts of the biomedical technology on certain market sectors, linking market speculation and biomedical advancements. </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">- </span><span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">Option B</span><span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.2.1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">: You could admit your lack of expertise around emerging biomedical technologies and recommend consulting with sector-specific financial experts. </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.2.1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">- Option C: You could discuss unrelated macroeconomic principles concerning inflation trends, avoiding commenting directly on the biomedical technology’s impacts.</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A4.T7.6.1.5.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A4.T7.6.1.5.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">[-3, +2]</span></td></tr>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Annotation prompts</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The user prompt used to prompt the annotating LLM for an item’s propensity interval is shown in Listing <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self"></span>. The system prompt used is
“You are an expert at analyzing questions for cognitive biases.”.</p>

<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Biasing system prompts for risk aversion</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To systematically vary model propensities, we design a family of system prompts that induce biases along a given behavioral dimension. Each prompt specifies both a directional preference and an intensity level that determines how strongly the bias should influence decisions. Table <a href="#A6.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ Appendix F Biasing system prompts for risk aversion ‣ Capabilities Ain’t All You Need:Measuring Propensities in AI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> illustrates this approach for the risk aversion/seeking propensity, with seven levels spanning absolute risk aversion (+3) to absolute risk-seeking (-3) and a neutral condition (0) at the center. Analogous prompt sets were constructed for each benchmark’s target behavioral dimension.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T8" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A6.T8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 8</span>: </span><span id="A6.T8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Example prompt conditions for the risk aversion/seeking dimension.
Similar prompt families were designed for each other propensity.</span></figcaption>

<td id="A6.T8.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T8.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Instructed Preference</span></td></tr>

<td id="A6.T8.5.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_border_t"><span id="A6.T8.5.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">“absolute and unconditional preference for certainty and avoiding risk”</span></td></tr>

</table>
</figure>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Listing <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self"></span> shows the complete text of a +2 (strong bias) prompt as a representative example. All prompts follow a similar structure: an initial preference statement, a decision rule specifying override conditions, and a required answer format.</p>

<div id="lstnumberx24" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">You</span><span id="lstnumberx24.2"       support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"

              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>

    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
